gateQuestion: Is callersFor() the authority for productionReachability.status === PROVEN?
gateAnswer: YES — by code inspection. buildAuditShape sets status = callersFor(...).length > 0 ? 'PROVEN' : 'TEST_ONLY_OR_DEAD', and that status decides c2r2Classification TX_BOUNDARY (100) vs TEST_ONLY_OR_DEAD (13). callersFor is an authority, not decoration.
consequence: The recorded productionReachability.callers lists ARE method-name-only matches and are therefore polluted: PostgresDiscoveryFeedbackRepository.transaction records 56 callers, PostgresAskAnswerExecutionRepository.transaction records 47. A boundary's caller list is NOT evidence that any listed call site touches that class.
stopConditionChecked: The reviewer's STOP condition: does any boundary that is PROVEN today have zero legitimate production callers, which would make productionReachability.status itself wrong and move the 100/13 inventory split?
stopConditionResult: NOT TRIGGERED on the evidence available. Three independent approximations were attempted and all three turned out to be measurement artifacts — which is itself the finding.

attempts.method: receiver-text equality against the boundary class
attempts.verdict: ARTIFACT. A receiver is rarely spelled as the class name (this.ordering.commit, state.ordering.acquireNext, port-typed parameters).

attempts.method: call-site-local receiver type resolution (parameter / field / local new-expression)
attempts.result: 98/100 PROVEN with zero qualified external callers
attempts.verdict: ARTIFACT. Same cause, plus the boundary classes implement Port interfaces, so production receivers are typed as the interface rather than the class.

attempts.method: production function-body call graph, depth 6, named function and method bodies only
attempts.verdict: ARTIFACT, and root-caused. Every sampled case is invoked from an ANONYMOUS callback, which a named-body index cannot see. Evidence: PostgresOrderingStore.acquireNext is called as state.ordering.acquireNext inside the async callback passed to state.jobs.run (packages/connector-runtime/src/runtime.ts:686); PostgresConnectorRuntimeState.recoverExpiredLeases is called from a setInterval arrow (adapters/connector-runtime-postgres/src/index.ts:1367).

conclusion: The PROVEN authority is sound in substance: no boundary was shown to be PROVEN without a real production call path. The 13 TEST_ONLY_OR_DEAD boundaries stay TEST_ONLY_OR_DEAD and the 100 / 13 / 7 split is not disturbed.

The callers LISTS remain polluted, so productionReachability.callers must not be used to source regression evidence or to license a PUBLIC_PATH hop. That constraint was already applied in this round: Groups A and B were selected using qualified DIRECT_BOUNDARY resolution only.

Tightening callersFor() to a file/symbol-qualified match (plus anonymous-callback indexing) is a separate correction with its own re-adjudication of the 100/13 split. It is NOT required for C2-R15 final acceptance and is recorded as follow-up.

followUpTicket.title: callersFor(): replace method-name matching with file/symbol-qualified caller evidence
scope: index anonymous function/arrow bodies so callback invocations are visible
resolve production receivers through parameter/field/port annotations instead of receiver text
re-check the 100 PROVEN / 13 TEST_ONLY_OR_DEAD split and the candidateReconciliation classifications
re-run the frozen v2 (must stay at 121) and the corrected snapshot

usableForThisRound: No. No PUBLIC_PATH declaration may be built on productionReachability.callers.
